summary: Iteration 29 — Sequential per-company ticket_number + webhook idempotency. Backend pytest: 7/7 PASS new + 16/16 PASS regression iter28 = 23/23 (100%). Validated: (1) POST /api/crm/tickets returns ticket_number (int, >=1001, contiguous +1); GET /api/crm/tickets/{id} exposes it. (2) backfill ran on startup — every ticket in GET /api/crm/tickets has ticket_number (int, >=1001). (3) Webhook POST /api/channels/webhook/message creates ticket with sequential ticket_number when phone is new; (4) when an OPEN ticket already exists for that phone, no new ticket is created — message is appended; identical wa_message_id replays are also deduped. (5) 8 concurrent POST /api/crm/tickets produce 8 unique ticket_numbers (counters.next_sequence is atomic via find_one_and_update + $inc). (6) Per-company isolation indirectly verified: CRM company sequence stays contiguous +1 across calls (counter doc keyed by `${company_id}:tickets`). (7) Regression CRUD + add-message preserves ticket_number on update. Iteration 28 regression remains 100% green.
critical_code_review_comments: counters.py next_sequence: returns start+seq where seq is the AFTER-inc value. With start=1000 and a freshly-created counter (seq=1) the first ticket is #1001 — correct. But if the counter doc already exists from a prior `next_sequence(name='tickets', start=0)` call (e.g. if someone reused this helper), the offset would double-add. Today only next_ticket_number reaches it with start=1000, so safe — but worth a code comment that `start` must be stable per-counter-name.

server.py backfill_ticket_numbers: scans tickets sorted by created_at then assigns numbers via next_ticket_number. Race-safe under restarts but if the backend is restarted while another instance is running, both will increment — could produce gaps but never collisions. Acceptable.
channels_routes.py webhook_message line 551: ticket lookup uses {status: {$nin:['fechado']}} — matches the spec ('NÃO criar novo ticket quando status != fechado'). Confirmed.

channels_routes.py webhook_message: when ticket is closed and same phone messages again, a NEW ticket is created with a NEW ticket_number. This is correct per spec but worth highlighting in product docs (each customer can have multiple historical tickets).

crm_routes.py POST /tickets: `ticket_number` is allocated BEFORE insert_one. If insert_one fails (e.g. duplicate id), the counter has already incremented, leaving a permanent gap. Low risk in practice; consider compensating decrement on failure if gaps become an issue.
crm_routes.py run_campaign sync path (line ~722) also calls next_ticket_number for each new ticket — correct; campaign-driven tickets are numbered in the same per-company sequence (intended).

rca of the issue: No issues found. Both reported bugs are fully addressed at the backend layer: (1) sequential ticket_number via atomic find_one_and_update on counters collection (race-safe, per-tenant); (2) webhook ticket idempotency via {customer_phone, status!=fechado} lookup before insert. The @lid microservice fix was applied in Node.js (out-of-scope locally) and could not be exercised end-to-end here, but the Python receiver correctly dedupes whatever phone the microservice forwards.
